title: Suite 128 (13'3" x 9'3" room) and Suite 114 (10'10" x 9'10" and 10'11" x 9'10" rooms) — real-estate plans, no booth placed
anchor: each room's own stated plan label (128.pdf 'ROOM 13'3" x 9'3"'; 114.pdf '10'10" x 9'10"' and '10'11" x 9'10"'), scaled per axis from 300 dpi renders of the raster plan; plans carry 'SIZES AND DIMENSIONS ARE APPROXIMATE'
interpretations: Both plans are Matterport-style raster floor plans with a size label per room and no wall chains. The labels are recorded as stated; everything else (jog, door positions and widths, hinges, partition) is scaled from the drawing and recorded as assumed with its scale.

Suite 128: the label is rotated vertical. Interior reads 648 px N-S by 444 px E-W at 300 dpi (ratio 1.46); 13'3" x 9'3" is ratio 1.43, the swap would be 0.70 — so 13'3" is N-S and 9'3" is E-W. Scales: N-S 4.075 px/in, E-W 4.000 px/in (the two disagree by 1.9%, inside the plan's 'approximate' disclaimer).

Suite 128: the room is not a rectangle. The powder room's north-east corner cuts into the room's south-west: the west wall steps east 83 px (20 3/4") at 230 px (56 1/2") below the north wall. 9'3" is read as the full width of the north part and 13'3" as the full north-south depth on the east side — both bounding dimensions.

Suite 114: labels horizontal. West room 410 px E-W by 375 px N-S (ratio 1.09 vs 130/118 = 1.10, swap 0.91) so the first number is E-W. West room E-W 3.154 px/in; east room E-W 3.099 px/in (406 px — the drawing makes the '10'11"' room 4 px narrower than the '10'10"' one); both rooms N-S 3.178 px/in.

Suite 114: the two rooms share one partition 22 px thick (about 7"), with north and south interior faces on the same lines (803.5 px and 1178.5 px in both rooms). They are placed with that true offset: east room origin = west room origin + 130" + 7". Wall thickness for these two rooms is 3 1/2" so the two rooms' walls meet inside the 7" partition instead of overlapping.

Layout between suites is arbitrary: Suite 128 is placed at x=420", Suite 114 from x=700", clear of the existing 'Room' group already in the model (x -184" to 304"). The two suites are different buildings; their relative position means nothing.
No ceiling height on either plan — 8'-0" house default, the open question that disqualifies booths fastest.
